::: {.callout-note}
## Relevant Learning Standards

10. Create effective data visualizations across multiple chart types (line, scatter, histogram, Q-Q plot), applying appropriate aesthetic choices such as color, grouping, and labeling. (Labs 1, 3, 4, 5)
11. Produce and interpret confidence interval plots that enable visual comparison of means and uncertainty across groups or time periods. (Lab 3)
12. Visualize spatial data using appropriate mapping tools, selecting suitable classification schemes and cartographic elements to support clear communication. (Labs 2, 3, 4, 6)
13. Arrange and present tabular results in a readable format appropriate for a technical document or report. (Labs 1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
:::

# Readings
* [Chapter 3 of Data visualization: A Practical Introduction](https://socviz.co/03-ggplot-basics.html) by Kieran Healy
* [R Graphics Cookbook](https://r-graphics.org/){target="_blank"}: Really this whole book is relevant--find what interests you!
* [Chapter 9 of Geocomputation with R](https://r.geocompx.org/adv-map). Be aware that tmap v.4 has significant changes over v.3, so you may need to adapt some things from this text.
